title: Exceptional Points revealed by the integrated imaginary scattering eigenphase
abstract: We propose and analytically demonstrate that the eigenphases of the scattering matrix provide direct, phase-sensitive signatures of exceptional points in open PT-symmetric systems. Using a one-dimensional PT-symmetric quantum dimer with balanced gain and loss, coupled to continuum leads, we track the evolution of the scattering eigenphases across the PT-exact to PT-broken transition. The imaginary parts of the eigenphases develop localized structures of opposite sign as the exceptional point is approached, reflecting the emergence of gain/loss asymmetry in the scattering eigenmodes. We introduce the integrated imaginary scattering eigenphase G(gamma), which condenses this information into a single experimentally accessible scalar. G(gamma) is negligibly small in the PT-exact phase and undergoes a sharp transition -- a pronounced inflection followed by saturation into a plateau -- near the exceptional point. The inflection point of G(gamma) precedes gamma_{EP} and coincides with the maximum amplitude of the transmission resonances, revealing that peak gain/loss asymmetry and eigenstate coalescence are governed by independent conditions in open systems -- a direct fingerprint of their finite coupling to the continuum. Because the analysis is formulated entirely at the level of the S-matrix -- without reference to any specific physical realization -- the results are universally applicable across wave systems, including photonic, acoustic, and microwave platforms where phase-resolved measurements are available.
summary: The paper introduces the integrated imaginary scattering eigenphase $G(\gamma)$ as a novel, global diagnostic tool to detect Exceptional Points (EPs) in open PT-symmetric systems. By analyzing the S-matrix eigenphases, it shows that $G(\gamma)$ exhibits a unique inflection point preceding the EP, confirming that peak gain/loss asymmetry and state coalescence are governed by distinct physical conditions in open environments.
main_problem: To find a direct, phase-sensitive signature of Exceptional Points (EPs) in open PT-symmetric systems that does not rely on identifying individual resonant states.
main_result: The integrated imaginary scattering eigenphase G(gamma) provides a robust global diagnostic for EPs; its inflection point precedes the EP and coincides with maximum gain/loss asymmetry, demonstrating independent physical mechanisms.
method: Analysis is performed entirely at the level of the Scattering Matrix (S-matrix), tracking the evolution of complex scattering eigenphases ($	heta_n$) across the PT-symmetry-breaking transition.
model_or_system: The model is a one-dimensional PT-symmetric quantum dimer with balanced gain and loss, coupled to continuum leads. The analysis is formulated generally for any wave system describable by an S-matrix (photonic, acoustic, microwave).
key_observables: Scattering Matrix elements ($r, t, r', t'$), complex scattering eigenphases ($	heta_n$), and the integrated imaginary scattering eigenphase $G(\gamma)$.
important_parameters: The non-Hermitian strength parameter $\gamma$, which controls the transition from PT-exact to PT-broken symmetry.
main_assumptions: The analysis is formulated entirely at the level of the S-matrix, making the results universally applicable across different wave systems.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the evolution of transmission resonances (Fig. 2) and track resonance positions/widths vs. $\gamma$ (Fig. 3). Crucially, they show the imaginary parts of eigenphases ($	heta_{Im, n}$) developing localized structures of opposite sign near EP (Fig. 5), and plot $G(\gamma)$ showing its characteristic inflection point before saturation (Fig. 6).
paper_structure: The paper introduces the S-matrix formalism for open PT systems, analyzes the complex eigenphases ($	heta_n$) as a diagnostic tool, develops the global scalar observable $G(\gamma)$, and finally demonstrates that $G(\gamma)$ robustly pinpoints the EP by tracking its unique inflection point.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful, model-independent spectroscopic technique for characterizing non-Hermitian degeneracies (EPs) in open quantum systems using only phase measurements, which is highly relevant to modern photonics and metamaterials research.

figures.caption: FIG. 1: (Color online) Diagram of the studied dimer composed of two scattering units, each composed of three potential barriers. The potential of the outer barriers of each scattering unit is real, while the potential described by the central barrier is complex. The sign of the imaginary part of the central barrier gives rise to loss (blue region) or gain (red region). This system is invariant under the combined action of parity and time reversal, and is therefore PT-symmetric.

FIG. 2: (Color online) Log-scale transmission spectrum as a function of energy in which only the first doublet of the dimer is plotted. Dimer parameters, for this and subsequent figures, are a = 1.15 nm, b = 2c = 0.02 nm, Vb = 50 eV, and V ′ = 0 eV. (a) For the Hermitian case (γ = 0) the maximum values of the resonances are found at E1,1 = 0.2086 eV (the first subscript refers to the associated doublet while the second one refers to the associated resonance), and E1,2 = 0.2615 eV. For γ = 0 the resonances have a unit amplitude and a maximum separation. As we increase the value of γ the separation between the resonances decreases and their amplitudes increases before the EP as it is observed...

FIG. 3: (Color online) (a) Evolution of the scattering resonances of the PT-symmetric dimer as a function of γ. The real part (upper panel) tracks the resonance positions: for γ = 0 the doublet is maximally separated due to level repulsion, and the separation decreases monotonically until both resonances coalesce at the exceptional point. Just below γEP only the lower- energy resonance is numerically resolvable, which accounts for the gap in the higher-energy trajectory. Beyond the EP a single merged resonance persists.
